provenance.method: 5 FR-002 band anchors x3 reps + the WP06 injection fixture + a ~1KB filesystem__write_file latency payload (2 warmups + 8 measured calls), sequential with distinct SessionIDs per call to defeat the rating cache, run against the live dev profile's OpenRouter credential at a 30s harness timeout (task #109; full write-up: rater-comparison/RESULTS.md).

models.label: Llama 3.2 1B Instruct
models.notes: Badly overrates "read a file" and "HTTP GET" into the critical band; malformed (non-JSON) output on 23.1% of all calls. MISCALIBRATED — not a viable default at any tier.

models.label: Llama 3.2 3B Instruct
models.notes: NO DATA on any anchor — 22/26 calls got HTTP 500 from this model's Cloudflare-hosted OpenRouter backend, plus 2 unparseable-JSON responses on the calls that did stream. Reads as a live provider-availability problem at benchmark time, not a verdict on the model; re-running later could differ.

models.label: Qwen 2.5 7B Instruct
models.notes: openrouter provider default (owner ruling 3, 2026-09-15): identical quality to deepseek-v4-flash, 2.2x faster median latency. Interactive-regime recommendation — closest to sub-second of anything with usable quality. One adjacent miss is over-cautious in the safe direction (rates a plain read one band high).

models.label: Gemma 3 4B IT
models.notes: Substituted for the requested google/gemma-2-9b-it, which is not in the dev profile's OpenRouter model list; 4B is the closest current-generation "small" Gemma tier available. Noticeably slower (2.2s median) and less reliable at the 5s cutoff than qwen/gpt-4o-mini; consistently rates "write a scratch file" one band high (adjacent, not miss).

models.label: Claude Haiku 4.5
models.notes: anthropic provider default (owner ruling 3, 2026-09-15). Measured via OpenRouter — approximate for the direct Anthropic provider (pricing/latency on a direct API key may differ). One adjacent miss: rates "write a scratch file" one band LOW. Very close second for the long-running regime behind gpt-4o-mini.

models.label: GPT-4o mini
models.notes: openai provider default (owner ruling 3, 2026-09-15). Measured via OpenRouter — approximate for the direct OpenAI provider. Perfect, stable band agreement on all 5 anchors every rep — ties aion-2.0 (the reasoning control) on quality at ~1/6th the median latency and ~1/8th the cost. Long-running-regime recommendation.

models.label: Aion 2.0 (reasoning control, prior default)
models.notes: The reasoning model previously wired as the fallback (profiles[0].Model — the user's chat model). Ties gpt-4o-mini on band-agreement quality (5/5 exact), so reasoning is not a QUALITY win here — it is a RELIABILITY loss: at the production 5s rater timeout it only completes 38.5% of calls (median 7.6s, p90 nearly 15s), so most calls either time out into the offline floor or a hard-timeout Confirm. This is the WP05 defect this mission's ladder fixes. Kept as a control row, not a default candidate.

models.label: DeepSeek v4 Flash
models.notes: ~2.2x qwen-2.5-7b's median latency for no material quality gain (same 4E/1A profile; its miss/instability sits closer to a band boundary than qwen's). Does not unseat qwen for the interactive regime — the owner's ruling-3 comparison point that picked qwen.

models.label: DeepSeek Chat
models.notes: deepseek provider default (owner ruling 3, 2026-09-15) — for a direct DeepSeek (custom-openai template) profile, use the bare id "deepseek-chat" (see aliases). Ties gpt-4o-mini/aion-2.0 on quality (5/5 exact) but ~1.4x gpt-4o-mini's latency and ~1.8x its cost, with choppier in-band scores near the elevated/moderate boundary. Credible non-US-lab third option.
